title: Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 1) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change tax concession ownership tests, exempt specified disaster assistance from income tax and allow deductions for donations supporting eligible ethics education.
It would base relevant small business and share-exchange concession tests on ownership, while treating specified underlying owners as holding assets for tax purposes.
The disaster exemption would cover events from 3 January 2013 to 30 September 2013, and the ethics donation provisions would start on Royal Assent.
changes: Life insurance companies, superannuation funds and trusts would be covered by revised ownership-based integrity tests.
Specified beneficiaries, bankrupt individuals, companies in liquidation and security providers would be treated as asset owners under the relevant rules.
The Disaster Income Recovery Subsidy would become exempt for the specified disasters.
Eligible ethics education public funds would gain a new deductible gift recipient category, subject to charitable registration and tax endorsement requirements.
summary.affected: Affected groups include the specified asset owners, life insurers, superannuation funds, trusts, disaster subsidy recipients, ethics education funds and their donors.

divisions.question: Tony Smith by leave—I move coalition amendments (1) and (2), as circulated in my name, together: (1) Clause 2, page 2 (table item 4), omit the table item. (2) Schedule 3, page 11 (lines 1 to 10), omit the Schedule. As I outlined in my speech on the second reading, the coalition is moving to excise schedule 3 from this bill. Amendments (1) and (2) give effect to that. Let me reiterate a couple of things for the benefit of the shadow Assistant Treasurer, and I will deal with some of the points he made. As he articulated, this legislation seeks to introduce a whole new general category. Currently, there is one provider nationally in Australia and that is Primary Ethics. We note that the explanatory memorandum to the bill provides that New South Wales example as the only one, with no reference to any other state or territory. As I previously stated, this one provider has sought a listing and it was rejected by the current government. As Senator Cormann outlined yesterday, the coalition has no philosophical objection to ethics classes but did not think it was appropriate that we have this whole new category created at this point without proper consideration of all the issues. I want to point out a few things to the Assistant Treasurer regarding what he said in his long speech of rebuttal to our position on this. He first said that Mathias Cormann, our shadow Assistant Treasurer, had confirmed that we have no philosophical objection and yet he accused him of having a philosophical objection. The Assistant Treasurer will, quite predictably, cast any aspersions on any scrutiny but, when it comes to his conduct of tax laws amendment bills, he is the Captain Chaos of Assistant Treasurers. speeches.speaker: Tony Smith
speeches.brief: Outlined coalition support for two of three schedules in the Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 1) Bill, covering scrip-for-scrip rollover integrity rules worth $220 million in revenue and tax-free disaster recovery payments for events from 3 January to 30 September this year, but announced the coalition would move to remove the third schedule creating a new deductible gift recipient category for ethics education, preferring case-by-case listing.

speeches.speaker: David Bradbury
speeches.brief: Opposed the coalition's move to strip out schedule 3, arguing it would deny Primary Ethics, the only current provider of ethics-based instruction as an alternative to religious education in New South Wales schools, deductible gift recipient status, and said creating a general category under division 30 of the tax act was fairer than requiring specific parliamentary listing for each new organisation.
